messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed 3 customer flows hit a weird async handoff during a capacity spike. Gateway matched the route, then async reroute kicked in and a tenant header override ended up applied during the reroute, which caused two different owners to process different parts of the same user request. anyone seen this?
kevin: saw one similar on staging yesterday. my read: header override evaluation is happening after quota/capacity checks, so when async reroute decides to spill we re-evaluate headers and accidental "late override" wins.
sasha: can you grab a tiny log snippet?
maria: pasted logs below:
```
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 route_matcher.v2 matched route=/predict tenant=team-x
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 quota.check passed, lane=priority
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 async_reroute.start reason=gpu_pool_surge
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 header_override=tenant-bypass=true evaluated=late
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 ownership_grant assigned=node-42
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 duplicate_handled conflict=node-17,node-42
```
ben: sounds like a pipeline ordering bug. two options: 1) evaluate header overrides in the pre-match phase so they influence lane selection, or 2) attach override tokens to request context earlier so reroute honors earlier decision instead of re-evaluating.
zoe: console/UX angle — we have customers using header overrides as an "escape hatch" during outages. If we change ordering we need clear console feedback: show when an override was accepted vs rejected and whether it was applied pre- or post-reroute. otherwise they'll think we silently dropped their override.
kevin: agree re telemetry. we should emit events: route.override.requested, route.override.bound, route.override.applied, route.fallback.invoked, circuitbreaker.triggered. fields: tenant_id, request_id, match_version, lane, owner_node, override_scope (tenant|route|session).
sasha: i'll add those events to the gateway trace span and include a short flag to annotate whether override was prebound. also canary plan: add featureflag gateway.header_prebind=true and route it to 10% traffic to test ordering change.
maria: can we also add a guard that prevents override from being able to bypass an active circuit-breaker unless the tenant is in a safelist? That seems safer than letting force overrides kill SLOs.
ben: yep — implement override modes: hard (bypass CB), soft (record intent, but still respect CB), and audit-only (log + console warning). default to soft.
zoe: console copy suggestion: "Force route override — may increase SLO risk. Choose Soft to request override without bypassing safety nets or Hard to force immediate routing (requires explicit justification)." show a 2-click confirmation if Hard.
kevin: small config proposal for pipeline (pseudo):
```
pipeline:
  - prebind_headers
  - route_match
  - quota_check
  - lane_selection
  - cb_check
  - dispatch
  - async_reroute (no re-eval of header overrides)
```
That would make header overrides influence lane selection and CB checks consistent. async_reroute should only consult prebound metadata.
sasha: will implement prebind + telemetry. adding canary now: `ff.gateway.header_prebind=10%`
deploy-bot: canary started: gateway-cluster-a -> 10% traffic (flag gateway.header_prebind)
maria: thanks. action items: sasha to raise tiny PR with pipeline reorder + telemetry events, ben to add override modes and safelist, zoe to draft console copy and audit banner copy. i'll follow up with a short postmortem if this surfaces more variants. :thumbsup:
kevin: +1, please add a quick e2e in our test harness that simulates concurrent reroute + header-update so we don't regress.
sasha: adding tests now.
